blocks.content: Quiz: In git diff output, what does a line starting with - indicate?
Tap an option below to answer:
A new line that was added in the most recent change
New additions are marked with +. The - prefix marks the opposite — something that existed in the last commit and is now removed or replaced.
New additions are marked with +. The - prefix marks the opposite — something that existed in the last commit and is now removed or replaced.
A line that existed in the last commit and was removed or replaced in the current version
Correct. - lines (shown in red) represent the before state — what was in the last commit. + lines (shown in green) represent the after state — what replaced them.
Correct. - lines (shown in red) represent the before state — what was in the last commit. + lines (shown in green) represent the after state — what replaced them.
A comment automatically added by Git to explain the change
Git adds no explanatory comments to diff output. Every line reflects actual file content — either the before state, the after state, or unchanged context.
Git adds no explanatory comments to diff output. Every line reflects actual file content — either the before state, the after state, or unchanged context.
A file that was deleted entirely from the repository
A fully deleted file shows as a block of - lines covering the whole file. A single - line means one specific line was changed — not the entire file.
A fully deleted file shows as a block of - lines covering the whole file. A single - line means one specific line was changed — not the entire file.
